items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-12-09
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] What about now these people you associate with the Creole kind of music like Piku and the big guy, Lillian Nelson and so on.

ctx.x: Zeb played with him before. I had played with him. Zeb. Zeb. Uh, he had, uh, uh, uh, Maurice French, uh, uh, Papa French was a fan of him. The band was, uh, uh, singing a band. He was only. He also had the other uncle that played Bees only. Then in advance, uh, was sitting around putting a string Bees down. Everybody was hidden. Bees behind. Bees on. Like Chester. Jim Lillard. Jim Lillard. And many other. Jax. I knew he was good. He was good. I knew he did something.
What about now these people you associate with the Creole kind of music like Piku and the big guy, Lillian Nelson and so on. Did they all tend to play in one area of town like in the downhill?

No, I don't think so. I'll tell you about the Creole people in the audience was like this one. Put a little Espinay Street. Uh. From Seminole. I said Seminole. Going back to Broad. I said from Clayborne. Uh. Columbus Valley. Well. There were different kinds of people. Because they thought they were more important than the, the poor, the poor, the other guy. You see. So they, uh. Many times they would not hire others to talk with the citizens. Uh. But, uh. They would hire a leader of Abraham. He had a great, uh,…
